component: SGCS1 laptop Windows hardening build (UK MoD hardening mod kit)
failure_mode: Hardening policies only partly implemented: FIPS mode not enabled in Silvus settings, no encryption key present notification, software runnable from USB, USB access allowed, browser showed not secure on SSH/HTTPS checks.
contributing: Full LMUK guidance scope not carried into the build
Pen testing and customer approval loop (GCSS-76, GCSS-133) delayed closure

evidence.quote: it was noted that some policies for the windows hardening build may not have been implemented fully
FIPS Mode in Silvus settings not enabled, No user notification that Encryption key is present in the encryption key box
Implement new Window Hardened Build Image, deploy on SGCS1-109 -COMPLETE

team_root_cause: Engineering did not implement full scope of the guidance provided by LMUK
reasoning: The FAT checks listed specific policies missing from the hardened Windows image. A new hardened image was built, pen tested and released (GCSS-133), and the customer approved it. The gap is a configuration scope gap in the ground station build, which matches the team's root cause.

event: VXE 489 fuselage flying with the 408 center wing (battery, drop payload) transitioned to VTOL landing and the two front lift motors did not start for a few seconds; the aircraft pitched nose down, lost about 100 ft, recovered and landed normally.
component: 408 CW VTOL avionics (VTOL AP board and VTOL AP interface board 107-107306)
failure_mode: Front lift motors drew almost no power while commanded to full throttle from about 8848 to 8850 s; signal or power path to both front ESCs failed upstream of the boom harness split. Exact mechanism on the board not confirmed.
contributing: Nylon screw 100-102984 holding brass ballast weight 107-102859 sheared, weight scarred the AP interface board and dislodged R32
408 CW was not inspected or RMA'd after an earlier hard landing (VIT2-193)
VTOL logs on the SD card were corrupted, so ESC level data was not available

evidence.quote: The front motors, 1 and 2, were making no power at 8848 when the rears turned on. Vtol current is very low while the front throttles are railed from 8848-8850.
Here is data from running both forward lift motor/ESC assys on the dyno. Both have similar responsiveness and performance to that of an Iron Bird motor/ESC assy.
The nylon screw (p/n: 100-102984) that fastens the ballast weight (p/n: 107-102859) to the red AP interface board broke free, likely due to vibration.
From our testing, the weight did not interfere with Servo lines 1 or 2. It also did not interfere with the Ethernet traces on T4 that I had suspected before.
Highly likely that problem occurred before the signals physically split apart from each other which would be on the VTOL avionics
Contrary Finding in Analysis: The observed Loss of Ethernet Connectivity occurs significantly after the pitch and roll events that cause altitude loss.

team_root_cause:
Two possibilities exist:
- Likely:
Quality or design issue: VTOL controller mass damping bar (brass bar) detached, causing shorts, and damaging the circuit board.
- Much less likely:
Simultaneous issue with both front Lift Motors/ESCs or chip hardware issue impacting only the front two.

would_settle_it.file: 408 CW VTOL AP board and interface board 107-107306
would_settle_it.what: Scope the SERVO1 and SERVO2 PWM outputs and front ESC supply on the bench while pitching and vibrating the board, to find what blocked the front motors
Recovered or decrypted VTOL logs showing ESC telemetry and PWM output for motors 1 and 2 at 8848 to 8852 s

reasoning: XCOMM data show both front motors commanded to full throttle but drawing almost no current while the rears ran, then recovering. Both front motor/ESC assemblies tested normal on the dyno, and a failure in two separate boom harnesses at once is unlikely, which points to the shared VTOL avionics in the 408 CW. A sheared ballast screw had let the brass weight scar the interface board, which is the team's likely cause, but bench tests could not show the weight interrupting the servo or Ethernet lines, so the exact mechanism stays open.
notes: Motor numbers come from ENG-3040 ('The front motors, 1 and 2') and Kurt Burian's 'motor 1, FL'. During dyno testing motor 2 (front right) from 408 was overrun at 95% throttle and failed; the team judged this unrelated. VA-1030 and VA-391 were canceled with no further work. Ethernet losses found in the logs did not line up in time with the pitch-down.

event: During TIQUILA FAT, VXE 510 (fuel cell configuration, 510 center wing) was on a launch wizard lift rotor check when the rear left rotor started, stopped and the system disarmed; a VTOL AP watchdog reset was found.
failure_mode: VTOL AP watchdog reset during the lift rotor check caused an automatic disarm; candidate causes are blocking in sensor polling or lower priority tasks blocking higher priority tasks.
contributing: Conformal coat intrusion on the 107-107306 interface board connector, judged not related
RTV seal under the interface board missing

evidence.quote: When checking the rear left rotor, it initially began to spin but stopped and system automatically disarmed.
Preliminary analysis showed that a watchdog reset occurred.
THIS IS WHAT THE CUSTOMER REPORTED BUT IS NOT TRUE, THE ABOVE INCIDENT WAS THE RESULT OF A BAD HLB
Hardware inspection revealed conformal coat quality issue, but initial assessments indicate that it is not related  to the watchdog timer event.
Issue in sensor polling (seen in 6 of 6 watchdog cases, unclear if this is symptom or cause)
Swapping centerwing to other aircraft (511 in battery configuration), lift rotor check was okay.

would_settle_it.what: VTOL AP event log crash dump and task trace at the disarm, to show which task blocked the watchdog

would_settle_it.file: Avionics Board Assy SN APB-1-1288 in HIL S-S100044
would_settle_it.what: HIL results with the original board pair, to separate a board specific fault from a general firmware fault

reasoning: The ticket and its master ticket VXEP-41 say a VTOL AP watchdog reset caused the disarm during the rotor check. The VXEP-41 root cause field lists only candidate software mechanisms (sensor polling, task priority blocking), none confirmed, and the conformal coat defect found was judged unrelated. The fault followed the 510 center wing (the check passed on another aircraft), so a board specific trigger cannot be ruled out.
notes: Canceled as a duplicate of VXEP-41, which was read. The customer's original description of a launch abort 6 inches off the stand is marked in the ticket as wrong and due to a bad HLB (likely the VXE 511 event in VXEP-12). The rotor checked was rear left (motor 4 by VXEP-272 numbering) but the fault is not motor specific, so position is left empty. FS2 epics read hold only task lists, no findings.

event: During Stalker FAT, VXE 509 completed the pre-launch wizard but on arming after lunch the fixed wing autopilot failed and the vehicle lost connection, so the launch was scrubbed on the ground.
failure_mode: Solder ball and FOD under the RF shield bridged a circuit to the shield ground, pulling the 3.3 V and 5 V rails down to 2.7 V and 2.5 V, so the FWAP lost the board and stopped communicating.
contributing: Header hand soldered by Edge and no inspection before RF shield close-out
Board without serial or lot label, from a rushed rework batch
Voltage gradient corrosion along the shield and 12 V rail

evidence.quote: The incident maggacc board 3.3V test point is showing 2.7V. The 5.0V test point is showing 2.5V.
there was a small spark around R1. After powercycling the board it was noted that the 5V and 3.3V test points were back to their correct values.
Why 3 –FOD (solder ball) was found inside RF Shield which bridged connections
Solder ball missed by Technician prior to close out of RF Shield
Noticeably, there is the most corrosion along the shield - which is connected to GND - and the 12V rail. This is indicative of voltage gradient corrosion.
The RF Shield was removed from all Qty 17 andno solder balls were foundon any other boards

team_root_cause: Quality issue.  Excessive solder balls, F.O.D. and potential corrosion was found on the component side of the magacc2 board (1710P01A), potentially as a result of missed quality check. This caused a short that inhibited functionality of the board.
reasoning: Test points on the removed MAGACC2 board read 2.7 V and 5.0 V rail at 2.5 V; after a spark near R1 cleared a bridge the board worked again. Opening the RF shield showed a solder ball and FOD bridging to the grounded shield, and the 8D traces it to a hand-soldered header not inspected before shield close-out. The other 17 boards from the same lot were clean, supporting a one-off workmanship defect.
notes: Ticket title says 'First Flight' but the failure happened on the ground before launch. AC 509 had two earlier Green AP replacements (NCR 1022, NCR 1165) that the team judged not related. VXEP-68 was moved from VA-473 and holds no findings.

event: On 27 April 2023 at a demo, VXE 407 (battery, drop payload) started its vertical landing when the VTOL autopilot hung; the lift motors stopped, the aircraft dived, flew an emergency pattern on the fixed wing autopilot for about 50 s, then landed vertically without damage.
component: VTOL AP firmware (event log write to microSD, in-flight watchdog handling)
failure_mode: VTOL AP became task locked (crash dump trace points at the event logging function writing to the microSD card) and, by design, the watchdog was cleared instead of resetting the processor because the aircraft was flying, so the VTOL AP stayed hung for about 50 s.
contributing: Watchdog logic in wdTaskTest() suppresses reset while flying
Possible microSD card or SPI hardware fault on the red VTOL AP board, not confirmed

evidence.quote: It looks like the VTOL controller reset during the transition and the fixed wing autopilot took over.
In the trace of the task lock it appears that it was hung on writing the event log.
In wdTaskTest() the func allows the WD to cause a system reset if the plane isnt flying. However, it allows the WD to be cleared because the plane was flying.
Upon full visual inspection of VTOL AP and VTOL AP interface boards, found no non-conformities.
Unable to replicate, seems to be problem in the VTOL AP.

team_root_cause:
Current assess this is the same WD issue as https://jenaero.atlassian.net/browse/VXEP-41 
Please see that issue for status (will be copied here on completion or if difference discovered.

would_settle_it.what: VTOL event log crash dump and task timing around 944 s, to confirm the event log write hang
HIL run of the quarantined board with microSD stress to reproduce the hang and separate SD hardware from firmware
Original shared investigation and the SharePoint timeline document VIT2-291 v407.docx

attachments_read: 23116_RMA Repair Quote for AC 407 Bench Repair Warranty LM 9-13-2024.pdf.md
reasoning: The VTOL event log holds a forced watchdog report and crash dump, and the XCOMM log shows a landing abort for VTOL health fail. The engineers traced the hang to the event logging function and found that the watchdog was deliberately not allowed to reset the processor in flight. Power delivery and board inspection found nothing, and the hang could not be replicated, so the cause is narrowed to the VTOL AP with software the leading candidate and the microSD hardware an open alternative.
notes: Description says all four VTOL motors stopped; the ENG-2990 witness says the rotors spun and then aborted. The ticket's Root Cause only points to VXEP-41, whose root cause is also a list of candidates. The intake PDF has no text. RMA-122: LM made 407 a ground test asset with a new avionics box and center wing. VXEP-41's attachment covers AC 510, not 407.

event: During TIQUILA FAT, VXE 511 had an aborted VTOL takeoff with all four lift motors cutting about 6 inches above the stand; it fell back onto the stand with minor fuselage damage, and a solder blob was found on the center wing VTOL power connector pins.
component: AS150 power contact (center wing dual current sense assy 107-102264 to HLB)
failure_mode: Contact had overheated on an earlier high-current flight and reflowed solder into a blob that kept the connector from fully mating; at launch the high-resistance partial mate let the lift battery voltage collapse below 18 V and the lift ESCs reset in a loop.
contributing: Earlier flight with much higher than normal lift current and power
Contact resistance 195 uohm on 511, above the 180 uohm criterion, possible poor contact plating
No latch or fully mated indicator; unlubricated O-ring can feel mated when not
Battery sealant squeeze-out at base of HLB AS150 connector blocks full engagement
HLB 2-1803 missing socket retention ring
Damaged 511 CW connector was not red tagged and was returned to flight

evidence.quote: In subsequent inspection, it was noted that the VTOL power connector would not fully engage due to a solder blob on the pins.
Drop in lift battery voltage to < 18V, steepest drop starts at 3416.3

From Carson: The root of the original incident could be the bent pins, resulting in only partial mating, generating far more heat than normal, which both melted solder and resulted in the voltage drop and non-flight.
Contact impedance measures 195uohms, which is over the newly established criteria of 180uohms.
when there is a gap and vibration is applied the current drops which can also lead to bad take off and landing
One of the 511 flights does seem to have much higher current and power than normal.

team_root_cause:

8D #24 - CW to HLB AS150 Connection Issues.pptx
Multiple potential causes:
- Incomplete mate of connector
- Quality issue.  Excess glue from sealing of battery prevents full engagement of the VTOL power connector, leading to increased internal resistance under high power load.  As a result, the connector pins overheat, potentially leading to solder flow and failure.
- Lack of latching connector, and fully mated indicator.
- If the connector O-ring not lubricated, the connector can seem fully mated without being so.
- High resistance contacts. 
- Over-current o

would_settle_it.what: Plot of the 511 flight with high current and power, to confirm it as the overcurrent event that reflowed the solder
SharePoint investigation report tying each flight and battery to the connector damage
Determination of the cause of the high lift current and power on 511

reasoning: Teardown found a solder blob on the CW VTOL power contact that stopped full engagement, and the logs show lift battery voltage dropping below 18 V with VT power faults as the motors cut. Bench tests on the same AS150 connector show a gap raises heating rate and that vibration on a partial mate drops current. The blob came from earlier overheating, which the team ties to an incomplete mate, a contact above the resistance limit and a high-current flight; all of these act at the same AS150 contact.
notes: Conflicting record of which center wing was on 511 at the FAT abort: VXEP-12 says the 516 CW, ENG-2181 (Greg Fryer) says the known damaged 511 CW was in play, and Sam Miller disputed that. Carson removed the solder blob before measurement, so the incident contact was not re-measured. The 516 CW launch wizard failure (June 2023, HLB 2-1801) is VXEP-13. The Vehicle Investigation decks include a template slide about v450 ESC 2 that is not this event; 'charts.docx' had no text; RMA intake PDFs have no text. VXEP-481 was moved from VA-82.

event: In June 2023 training at Helendale, VXE 511 fuselage with the 516 center wing and HLB 2-1801 failed the launch wizard motor check after one earlier flight (rotors turned only half a turn, HLB voltage fluctuating 7 to 27 V); the flight was canceled and the CW power connector was discolored.
component: AS150 anti-spark power contact (516 CW dual current sense assy 107-102264)
failure_mode: Contact overheated from high lift current and/or a partial mate; anti-spark resistor damaged (96.9 ohm against about 6 ohm normal), contact resistance 313 uohm against a 235 uohm limit, giving an intermittent HLB connection under load.
contributing: Overcurrent seen in the logs of the previous flight
Connector possibly not fully mated
Left wing connector also showed melted solder

evidence.quote: The VTOL control menu shows significant fluctuations in the HLB.
Shows damage at the top of anti-spark contact. , Resistance across the resistor measured at 96.9 ohms. usually ~6ohms.
There is an overcurrent in the logs; can be caused by not fully connecting.
Left wing connector also shows black residue and melted solder, which indicates overheating and high current.
Tested 516’s AS150 contact, measured 313 uOhms (>235 uOhms is failure). Anti-spark now measuring ~178 ohms.
Dual Current Sense SN 1125 was tested by Engineering and it passed

team_root_cause:
Intermittent connection to battery, likely caused by overheating due to connector not being fully plugged in. 
See https://jenaero.atlassian.net/browse/VXEP-12 
511+516-investigation report.pptx
8D #24 - CW to HLB AS150 Connection Issues.pptx

would_settle_it.what: VTOL00029 lift current and HLB voltage on the prior flight, to separate overcurrent from a partial mate
Wear marks on the contact showing how far the HLB connector had been inserted

reasoning: The HLB voltage swung 7 to 27 V during the motor check and the CW high voltage connector was discolored. Measurements on the 516 CW found a damaged anti-spark resistor and an AS150 contact far above the resistance limit, and the previous flight's logs show overcurrent, so the failure is at the HLB to CW AS150 contact. Whether a partial mate or the high current started the overheating is not settled, so the initiating cause is left unknown.
notes: Corrective actions and most investigation are on VXEP-12. The dual current sense harness SN 1125 later passed an engineering test after cleaning (contact 188 uohm), which the team could not explain. HLB 2-1801 retest in Nov 2023 showed possibly unbalanced cells (VA-31), not followed up. VA-482 (VXE 553 solder blob, NCR 1481) is a separate similar event. VA-392 and VA-320 hold no content.

event: During STALKER FAT, D450+ fuel cell SN 510 failed during startup on the ground with fault code 17440, and rebooting did not clear it.
component: D450+ fuel cell cathode air blower (WS7040 COTS blower with PCA129 control board)
failure_mode: Cathode blower motor damaged by lock rotor at startup or unprotected high current draw (over 2.0 A), so the blower did not respond (fault 17440).
contributing: PCA129 blower control software lacked lock rotor and current protections
Initial software validation did not test these failure modes
Damage can occur in QC and only show on a later cycle

evidence.quote: Once it was replaced with a new blower, the system functioned as intended.
The cause is determined to be either lock-rotor failure or a unprotected high power draw that damaged the blower motor.
Fault Code 17440 reports a non-responsive Cathode Air Blower.
Blower software lacked necessary features to protect COTS blower from Lock Rotor and High Current Draw Failures.
In failures, Blower can be observed exceeding 2.0A current draw.

team_root_cause:
Software issue.  Cathode fan calibration values did not cover all failure modes.
[embedded: image-20231108-034415.png]

See TPTR-58_EAES 8D Failure Analysis_10.9.2023.pptx
reasoning: The failure was reproduced at Ann Arbor and cleared by replacing the cathode blower, a direct swap test. The 8D shows fault 17440 means a non-responsive cathode blower and that the PCA129 blower software lacked lock rotor and high current protection, with failed blowers drawing over 2.0 A. The team's 'calibration values' wording is the same software cause; the failed part is the blower motor.
notes: The 8D is titled TPTR-58 but covers this TPTR-88 event. The 8D lists RC1 (lock rotor or high current at startup) and RC2 (blower damaged in Ann Arbor QC, failing after delivery); the ticket does not say which applied to SN 510. Aircraft tail not given (fuel cell serial 510 only).

event: During FAT, conformal coat was found inside connectors on VTOL AP interface boards (first on AC 510, then AC 509 and AC 511); no flight failure was tied to it.
failure_mode: Conformal coat intruded into connector pins because the RTV seal applied under the board was not on any drawing, BOM or procedure and was skipped, and inspection did not catch it.
contributing: Inspection did not include a conformal coat check of the connectors

evidence.quote: Whilst not identified as a flight issue, the full impact of the issue is not known.
That sealing step does not appear to be captured on any drawing, BOM, or procedure even though it is critical to getting a successful product.
Based on this info we disassembled the board assy so we could look at the connector pins on the 107-107306 Interface board and we found conformal coat instrusion.
AC 509 and AC 511 centerwings were also brought back to SLO Final Assy and found to have conformal coat in the same connectors on the interface board.

evidence.file: data/vxep/VXEP-130/attachments/15767_AC 510 VTOL AP Board Investigation - MP 23.08.09.pptx.md
evidence.quote: Bad – conformal coat present inside and around connector

team_root_cause: Poor application of Conformal Coating and Failure in Quality Inspection
reasoning: Inspection of the AC 510 avionics board against a new one found the RTV seal missing under the interface board and conformal coat inside the connectors under black light; AC 509 and AC 511 had the same defect. VXEP-130 records that the sealing step was never on the drawing, BOM or procedure. This is the same cause as the team's, with the missing process step and the affected part named.
notes: Ticket names no aircraft; tails 510, 509 and 511 come from VXEP-41. The comment's VA-165 was moved to VXEP-130. The defect was found while investigating the 510 watchdog event (VXEP-9/VXEP-41) and was judged unrelated to it.

event: On 26 June 2023 at Helendale training, VXE 493 drifted rearward during vertical descent in strong wind and landed short of and downwind of the planned landing zone, without damage.
failure_mode: Wind at or above the 20 mph launch and recovery limit pushed the aircraft backward during VTOL descent; nudging forward lowered wing lift and the aircraft dropped, so nudge was stopped.
contributing: FDR not downloaded, so high-rate VTOL logs for the event are missing
Possible limits of the FW helper control loops in high wind (FS2-1392, not evaluated)

evidence.quote: It appears that the wind was at or above the 20mph limit for much of the approach which probably contributed to the rearward drift.
We were unable to reproduce this issue in our HILSim as it does not accurately  model VTOL flight conditions above 20mph.
It was indeed windy just within the tolerance and limitations for take-off and landing around 15kts
It is unclear because the data was not provided for the underlying incident. Data was provided for the wrong flight.
Data in a provided flight suggest winds and operation outside General Environmental Limitations may have been contributing factors.

team_root_cause: Winds (20-25mph) were above the specified limits for the vehicle (20mph),

would_settle_it.what: Wind estimate, position and lift throttle data for the 26 June landing (pack lacks full logs)
SharePoint analysis of the 1 Hz logs and wind

reasoning: The 1 Hz logs show wind at or above the 20 mph VTOL limit for much of the approach, and the observer and pilot describe a windy day with rearward drift. High-rate VTOL logs were never downloaded and the HIL cannot model wind above 20 mph, so a control-loop weakness cannot be excluded. The evidence narrows the cause to high wind at or near the limit, as the team concluded.
notes: Wind accounts conflict: pilot about 15 kts (about 17 mph) 'just within' limits, Daniel Lloyd near 20 mph, Root Cause 20 to 25 mph. The 1 Hz logs showed about 40 ft of drift against the 168 ft reported. FS2-849 mentions AV496, apparently a typo for 493.
